text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today, continuing a strong three-day rally that's lifted the stock nearly $42 since November 6th. The gain appears tied to the broader refining sector's benefit from tighter diesel and heating oil supplies: diesel & heating oil inventories sit at just 103.3 million barrels while refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year, which typically improves margins for refiners who produce these fuels.

However, the two-week decline of 6.76% reflects a headwind that today's bounce didn't fully erase: Russian crude production has rebounced to 8.73 million barrels per day and global oil markets have returned to surplus according to the IEA, which puts downward pressure on crude prices (currently $89.62 domestically) and narrows the profit margin refiners earn on each barrel they process.
